scope: Read-only re-review of T4-R1 through T4-R5 against phase-two-task-4-fix-package.json. The pending full extraction/evaluation publication gate and legacy apps.operations.services publication integration are excluded root integration work.

fix_verdicts.title: Project-candidate approval still trusts context supplied by the proposed definition
fix_verdicts.evidence: The fix binds UNIT candidates to candidate.standard_code and candidate.raw_term, and DictionaryRelease now persists an immutable non-PHI candidate_reviews summary. For PROJECT candidates, however, review_candidate calls proposed.match(candidate.raw_term, specimen=definition.get('specimen', ''), panel=definition.get('category', '')). Both context values come from the submitted definition, while the authorized source observation specimen available through candidate.sources is never compared. A URINE source candidate can therefore be accepted as a BLOOD definition merely by adding its raw term as an alias; the lookup is then performed with the proposed BLOOD context and resolves successfully. The added test removes the raw-term alias but does not exercise a source/definition context mismatch.
fix_verdicts.consequence: A reviewer with authorized access to one candidate can still approve a context-specific identity that the candidate evidence does not support, so the release provenance records a review without establishing that evidence-to-definition binding.
fix_verdicts.action: Read the specimen context from the authorized candidate sources and require it to agree with the accepted definition and resolution context. Because normalized_key already partitions candidates by observation.specimen, this can be checked consistently across the candidate's surviving sources. Add a negative test using a real source specimen that differs from the proposed definition specimen.

fix_verdicts.evidence: _checked_rules now validates kind-specific units and numeric prerequisites, resolves units against the reviewed definition, validates report_sum components against the composed dictionary, rejects self/duplicate components, and rejects duplicate rule IDs within a review. preview_dictionary rejects conflicting IDs across candidates and requires a new rule version when content changes. Parameterized malformed-rule tests and rule identity/version tests cover the material positive and negative paths from the finding.

publish_dictionary now requires expected_preview_hash, recomputes the preview after locking the candidates and publication row, and rejects any mismatch. The updated normal publication path supplies the preview hash and the stale-candidate-revision test proves rejection after re-review.

rollback_dictionary now requires expected_active_hash and checks current_dictionary().content_hash after acquiring the global publication lock. The new negative test exercises an expected hash that no longer matches the active release.

DictionaryRelease.save now treats indicator_count, candidate_reviews, published_by_id, and published_at as immutable along with the prior snapshot fields. Published rules have rules_hash and a release_hash binding the payload content hash to the rules digest, and dictionary_for_release/rules_for_version validate those hashes before use. Tests cover audit-field mutation and persisted-rule tampering.

confirmed_fixes: Candidate IDs, revisions, reviewer identity/time, definition hashes, and rule hashes are retained in the immutable release after source/candidate deletion.
Rule additions and replacements participate in preview diff, preview_hash, rules_hash, and release_hash.
Publication requires a reviewed preview and rollback requires an expected active payload identity.
All release audit fields except the active pointer are protected against ordinary model saves.
